etymologies.etymologyHTML: From neck +‎ lace.

definitions.definition: (jewelry) An article of jewelry that is worn around the neck, most often made of a string of precious metal, pearls, gems, beads or shells, and sometimes having a pendant attached.
(figuratively) Anything resembling a necklace in shape.
(South Africa) A device used in necklacing (an informal execution); a rubber tyre that is filled with petrol. It is placed around the victim's chest and arms, and set on fire.

quote.citation: 4 August, 2004, “Necklacing: 7 held”, in Headline Pretoria News:
quote.text: Seven people have been arrested in connection with Saturday's "necklace" murder of three men in the Tjokville informal settlement at Jeffrey's Bay.

quote.citation: 2000 Beyond Our Wildest Dreams: The United Democratic Front and the Transformation of South Africa by Ineke Van Kessel
quote.text: Several of the alledged witches in Apel and GaNkaone were also subjected to a necklace execution

quote.citation: 2004 A Human Being Died That Night: A South African Woman Confronts the Legacy of Apartheid by Pumla Gobodo-Madikizela
quote.text: In the fluidly unfolding events of a necklace murder, was there time and space to stop the killing?

definitions.definition: (South Africa) To informally execute by necklacing; by setting on fire a petrol-filled rubber tyre which has been put around the bound victim's neck.

quote.text: Frustrated residents tied the hands of two suspected criminals, put tyres around their necks and then set them alight. In a manifestation of growing disillusionment with the criminal justice system, residents of Bramfischerville, west of Johannesburg, on Tuesday abducted and necklaced two suspected burglars.

quote.citation: 2002 Buthelezi: A Biography by Ben Temkin
quote.text: Inkatha members have been hacked to death and necklaced, and their houses have been destroyed

quote.citation: 2000 Beyond Our Wildest Dreams: The United Democratic Front and the Transformation of South Africa by Ineke Van Kessel
quote.text: The first instance of necklacing occurred in March 1985 in the Eastern Cape township of KwaNobuhle.
